messages:
maria: Heads-up — nightly-eval (2026-03-19 03:00 UTC) shows a large regression on the finance promptset for rwd-3-small-int8.
chris: numbers?
maria: baseline rwd-3-fp16 EM=86.1, rwd-3-small-int8 EM=72.4, delta -13.7. Rouge/larger gen metrics also down. :warning:
lin: that is huge. did PTQ calibration finish? which quant config?
maria: using ptq-packedkv-v2, kv_stride=4, per-channel scale, no activation clipping. seq lengths in failing set skew >512 (lots of long docs).
sophia: QA-bot re-ran a quick diff and attached sample diffs.
qa-bot: sample diff snippet:
```
Q: "What's the total Q3 revenue..."
baseline: "$1.2B"
int8: "$1.2
$"  <-- broken tokenization/linebreaks
```
jake: that looks like token-boundary / kv-cache alignment to me — seeing wrapped tokens mid-number.
chris: could be packedKV stride mismatch under int8 codepath leading to misplaced KV offsets for long sequences. We've seen similar when stride != implementation expectation.
lin: I'll repro locally with synthetic long promptset and dump KV offsets. If it's stride mismatch we should reproduce quickly.
maria: repro steps I used:
```
python eval.py --model rwd-3-small-int8 --prompts finance_long.json --kv_stride 4 --batch 1 --seed 42
```
lin: running that now. bookmarked the eval job id (eval-3342).
dev-bot: started job eval-3342 on runner-ml-6 (ETA ~8m)
(6m later)
lin: I can reproduce. kv indices are shifting after the quant-packed serialization step — appears to drop a separator byte when packed into the int8 cache blob.
sophia: how does that explain string breaks?
lin: when offsets shift, decoder picks wrong start position for next chunk -> tokenization boundary misalignment -> inserted newline/garbled token. Effect visible only for sequences >512 which trigger multi-kv-chunk handling.
chris: root cause then: packedKV serialization bug in int8 packed path that mishandles chunk boundary for kv_stride=4 on sequences that produce >1 KV chunk. Not a tokenizer change.
jake: mitigation options: 1) rollback to previous packedkv serializer for nightly and canary, 2) gate int8-packedkv for seq>512, 3) fix serializer and add unit tests.
maria: recommend immediate rollback/gating for rwd-3-small-int8 in nightly and hosted canary. Also add gating rule to block any int8-packedkv variant when mean_seq_len > 400 in onboard harness.
sophia: agreed. I'll open a canary with rollback to ptq-packedkv-v1 (pre-serialization change) at 5% traffic for dedicated. chris, can you own the rollback?
chris: I will. I'll also open a PR to add the serialization assertions and a reproducer in runtime-tests.
lin: I'll build a minimal patch to serialization that correctly accounts for the chunk separator and add a regression test that runs the long-sequence synthetic that failed. Targeting patch by EOD.
jake: QA: I'll extend nightly-eval to include the failing anky finance_long prompt as a guardrail and set action to fail-on-EM-drop >8 points. Also adding tokenizer boundary checks (count of broken token boundaries).
maria: ownership summary:
- chris: rollback canary + patch PR (#5021) + coord with infra to deploy fallback
- lin: serializer fix + regression unit test + bench repro
- sophia: create canary rollout (5% dedicated) + monitor dashboard
- jake: eval harness update + gating rule (block int8-packedkv when mean_seq_len > 400)
- qa-bot: run extended nightly once rollback in place and report
chris: immediate actions I'll take now:
1) open rollback deployment for rwd-3-small-int8 to ptq-packedkv-v1 on overnight canary
2) create emergency gating rule in eval pipeline to mark this quant config unhealthy
3) link dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/eval-nightly?orgId=1&panel=12
maria: timeline expectations — rollback + gating by +30m, fix PR by EOD, deploy fix to canary next day, re-eval full promptset before unblock.
sophia: putting a temporary alert: nightly-regression-int8-packedkv on PagerDuty until resolved.
(assignment reactions)
chris: @lin please ping me on PR; I'll review fast-track.
lin: will do.
qa-bot: queued nightly rerun after rollback; job id queued-3343.
maria: thanks team. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
